==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|e'rywhere|e'erywhere|everwhere||US|dialectal}}
* {{alt|en|every where||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|eauerihwer}}, from {{der|en|ang|-}} {{af|ang|æfre|gehwær|nocat=1}}. {{surf|en|every|where}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɛv.ɹi.(h)weə(ɹ)/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɛv.ɹi.(h)wɛɹ/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-everywhere.ogg|a=US}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# [[in|In]] or [[to]] [[all]] [[location]]s under [[discussion]].
#: {{ux|en|He delivers the mail '''everywhere''' on this street.}}
#: {{ux|en|We went '''everywhere''' at the school - we talked to all the teachers in their classrooms.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=76
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21579801-making-sense-statistics-riddle-our-days-snakes-and-ladders Snakes and ladders]
|passage=Risk is '''everywhere'''. From tabloid headlines insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, of course, it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins. For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial|hyperbole}} In or to a few or more locations.
#: {{ux|en|We went to Europe last year and went '''everywhere''': Berlin, Paris, London, and Madrid.}}
#: {{ux|en|When I shop for shoes, I like to look '''everywhere'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I've looked '''everywhere''' in the house and still can't find my glasses.}}

====Antonyms====
* {{l|en|nowhere}}
